A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimal guaranteed performance is the same as the expected average performance, when the specular component is isotropic.

the min-capacity of a M /spl times/N multiple-antenna channel on a Ricean environment with a static specular is equal to the avg-capacity of a single-antenna channel with the same specular component, and that the optimal transmission scheme for the former is the same as the optimal transmission scheme in the latter.

the optimal performance for a multiple antenna wireless channel with a static deterministic component is equal to the average capacity of the channel with the deterministic component modeled as a random vector with isotropic distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a multiple- antenna compound channel, it is sufficient, for purposes of computing min-capacity or computing achievable rate regions, to optimize over the joint density over the magnitudes of the transmitted signals.

, in the presence of a specular component with unknown direction and unknown rank, the optimal strategy to maximize worst case capacity is to transmit independent signals on each antenna, with the transmitted signal magnitudes being independent and nonnegative.

the min-capacity and avg-capacity for a compound channel with M transmit and N receive antennas on a Ricean channel with a static rank-one specular component is equal to the avg-capacity for the compound channel with min{M, N} antennas on a Rayleigh channel with no deterministic component.
